subject: Custodial log rotation & ephemeral data accrual — clarifications for audit
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@healthex.com>

Cc: Healthex Compliance <compliance@healthex.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify log rotation / ephemeral accrual for upcoming SOC2 review

Hi Monica,

Planning our SOC2 readiness review next month and Security wants a short explanation of Redwood's log rotation and ephemeral log accrual for customer-facing requests. Two specific asks:

1) For tenant-level request traces and GPU inference logs (request metadata, timestamps, small KV caches) — what's the default retention, and how is rotation handled (s3 lifecycle? object expiry? rolling indexes?).
2) Do you have a documented customer-specific exception / waiver flow (we asked for a 120-day retention for forensics) and what evidence would Redwood provide (signed attestation, archived bundle, sample export)?

Can you point me to the SOPs or provide a short one-page summary we can attach to the audit packet?

Thanks,
Alan
Alan Cho
Director, IT Compliance
Healthex Medical Inc.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@healthex.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log rotation / ephemeral accrual for upcoming SOC2 review

Hi Alan — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below; I'll assemble a one-page summary and attach the SOP. Looping in Sean (infra) and Laura (security ops) for technical and attestation pieces.

1) Default retention: Tenant-level request traces and short-term inference logs are retained for 30 days by default. Rotation is implemented as a time-based lifecycle on our object store: logs are written to per-tenant prefixes, compacted hourly, and expired by lifecycle rule at 30 days. High-volume aggregated telemetry (non-PII metrics) is retained longer in compressed OLAP for analytics.

2) Customer exceptions: We support formal retention exceptions (aka custodial holds) on a per-account basis. The flow is: customer writes a request to compliance@redwood.com -> product/security triage -> authorized exception added to account config -> logs are retained to a locked archive bucket for the agreed window (e.g., 90/120/180 days). Evidence: we can provide a signed attestation plus a sampled archive bundle (SHA256 manifests) and a CSV inventory of preserved objects.

Attachments I will produce: short SOP + sample manifest.

Monica

Monica / team — technical clarifications:

- Default retention: correct — 30 days for request traces and short-lived inference artifacts. Logs are written to per-tenant prefixes in S3 (or equivalent object store in private deployments). We compact small records hourly to reduce object count and then rely on lifecycle expiry.
- Exception handling: we currently implement exceptions as a per-account retention override that moves copies of the relevant prefixes to an "account-locked-archive" bucket. For hosted customers we apply S3 Object Lock in GOVERNANCE mode plus bucket-level IAM restrictions and KMS keys scoped to the archive. For private/VPC installs we provide a documented procedure and recommend enabling server-side object lock with a customer-managed KMS key.
- Evidence package: we can export a zipped sample (log-sample-2026-06.zip) containing a manifest.csv with SHA256, plus the SOP pdf (sop-log-rotation.pdf). We also include an access log extract showing the archive creation event and the retention ACL change.

Notes / limitations: We do not currently provide a full immutable WORM guarantee across all private on-prem installs unless the customer enables object lock and KMS on their side; the attestation should reflect that we have controls in our hosted environment, and that private/on-prem customers must enable equivalent controls.

Happy to draft the one-pager.

— Sean
